look_here_first: An ANNUAL milkvetch with showy bicolored purple-blue and white pea flowers, short appressed hairs and slender curved/flattened pods, not a thick inflated groundplum fruit. Check the banner/wing/keel color pattern, leaflets and fruit cross-section.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local source; World Flora Online/WCVP currently recognize Astragalus lindheimeri.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; exact target-zone county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Fabaceae/Astragalus: alternate pinnate leaves, papilionoid pea flowers, and legumes; fruit shape, inflation, hairiness, and curvature are especially useful for species ID.
best_field_traits: annual with decumbent-to-ascending stems often under ~35 cm
fine appressed (strigose) leaf and stem hairs; avoid confusing this with densely silver-scaled leaves
several conspicuous purple-blue/white pea-type flowers clustered in short racemes
flattened curved-oblong pods generally ~17–27 mm long, NOT plump hairy balloon pods
separate from A. plattensis (large fleshy pubescent pod) and A. crassicarpus var. berlandieri (fleshy groundplum) by fruit form
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Previously marked perennial with inflated hairy pods in the provisional dataset; corrected against published Texas flora / Barneby: this is an annual with a flattened, curved-oblong pod. A. nuttallianus group shares smaller pea flowers and slim pods, so flower size and mature fruit shape both matter.

curation_status.taxonomic_visual_correction: 2026-10-13: corrected plant duration and fruit description using Botanical Research Institute of Texas Flora of North Central Texas / Barneby 1964; previous provisional text conflated the taxon with plump-podded Astragalus.
